newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks end off despite end to CANTV strike.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks end off despite end to CANTV strike.

text.p: Poor Venezuelan earnings and rattled U.S. markets continued to weigh on Caracas stocks, which closed off despite an end to telephone company CANTV's three-week strike, traders said.
"After the government's intervention, confidence has returned to the stock, which rose today," said one trader.

Striking CANTV workers returned to work Friday after the government ordered an end to their walk-out over pay contracts, saying the dispute would be settled by third party arbitration. No date has yet been set for settlement proceeding. The stock closed up 19.75 bolivars at 2020.00.
The bolsa's 19-share index closed down 0.32 percent at 6,133.83 points as 15 million shares traded worth 2.5 billion bolivars ($5.22 million).
Meanwhile, Merinvest's composite index, which includes CANTV, closed broadly flat at 94.16 points. Among traded issues, 14 fell, 13 rose and seven ended flat.
"Volume was up a bit today, but there's no foreign bids at the moment," said Provincial broker Diogenes Saenz.
"Local investors are also feeling apathetic after disappointing first quarter company results, and Electricidad de Caracas's recently declared dividend that was less than good," he added.
Electricidad said Tuesday it would pay this year a three bolivar per share cash dividend plus a one share per 25 stock dividend.
